definition: Hyperdimensional computing (HDC) is an approach to computation.
details: HDC is motivated by the observation that the cerebellum operates on high-dimensional data representations. In HDC, information is thereby represented as a hyperdimensional (long) vector, which is called a hypervector. A hyperdimensional vector (hypervector) could include thousands of numbers that represent a point in a space of thousands of dimensions, as vector symbolic architectures is an older name for the same provided approach.

explainer.lead: Hyperdimensional computing represents information as very long vectors called hypervectors. It is motivated by the observation that the cerebellum operates on high-dimensional data representations.

tiers.eli5: It stores each idea as a very long string of numbers, so similar ideas end up with similar strings.
tiers.practitioner: Information is encoded as hypervectors of thousands of dimensions, with operations on them standing in for binding and combination. Pitfall: the approach is defined at a high level, so concrete accuracy and scaling depend heavily on the chosen encoding.
tiers.paperLevel: Data are represented as hyperdimensional (long) vectors, each containing thousands of numbers describing a point in a space of thousands of dimensions; vector symbolic architectures is an older name for the same approach. Limits: performance is tied to encoding design, and the stated motivation is biological rather than a formal guarantee.

explainer.example: A concept is stored as a vector of thousands of numbers, and combining concepts corresponds to operations on those vectors rather than on symbols.
